items.whoItHelped: Younger primary students working through a big project of their own for the first time.
items.whatSheLearned: Primary Prosperitas has helped me understand how to deal with different obstacles that come up across different situations. I've learned foundational project management skills like scheduling and time tracking, which help me finish projects efficiently.

updates.label: Primary Prosperitas -Start
updates.body: Mentoring students from Barnier, Hambledon, Nirimba Fields and Quakers Hill Public Schools through the 2026 Primary Prosperitas program — helping them shape a personal interest project, work out their own driving question, and set goals for it.

updates.label: Primary Prosperitas - End
updates.body: Our mentors and mentees came together for their final session before presenting their projects in Week 1 of Term 4. With presentation day fast approaching, students used the session to fine-tune their ideas, strengthen their delivery and make those final improvements to their projects. There was a wonderful sense of focus and purpose in the room as mentors supported their mentees and students prepared to share their work.

images.alt: Rithu sitting across a table from a primary school mentee, going through a worksheet together in the library
Rithu and her primary school mentee sitting side by side in the library, each wearing a name badge, with a laptop and an open project folder on the table between them

items.whatSheDid: Helping bring students' suggestions to the school and contributing to changes that affect everyone, including through Mini Vinnies. Being part of the SRC has also meant a full Leadership Day of workshops on public speaking, critical thinking and problem-solving, alongside smaller team moments like the SRC's Valentine's Day rose deliveries around the school.
items.whoItHelped: Fellow students, by giving them a voice in decisions that affect the school.
items.whatSheLearned: The Student Representative Council helped me learn practical leadership skills like how to advocate for my peers, and teamwork and communication. Being part of the SRC helped me build on being an advocate for my peers, because as a school student I can put myself in the shoes of my peers so that I can be the voice for the students and help bring change to the school. By being in the SRC I learnt the importance of teamwork, because teamwork is what pushes the SRC to make changes, negotiate solutions, and share peer feedback.

images.alt: Rithu wearing her Student Representative Council badge, listening alongside fellow SRC members during a Leadership Day workshop

items.whatSheDid: Helping students find books, running library activities, and writing book reviews for the library's own review series, The Library Lowdown. Recognised in the school's 2025 Library Crew celebration and awarded a Certificate of School Service for her contribution as a Library Monitor, now in her second year in the role.
items.whoItHelped: Students looking for their next read. Creating activities that students can enjoy during lunch and recess.
items.whatSheLearned: Being a library monitor helped me build skills like responsibility and basic public speaking. Library monitors aren't meant to stay only in the library — they're also involved in the wider school community, like helping Year 6 students transition smoothly from primary to high school. Whilst helping the Year 6 students transition, I learnt to deliver information to a large crowd of students, teachers and parents, and how to manage a large crowd.

images.alt: Rithu holding her 2025 Certificate of School Service, awarded for being a QHHS Library Monitor

items.whatSheDid: I enjoyed when I got to go into every classroom to get the tokens. At the end of each term all the tokens will be weighed and then the house that has the most weight will win and receive whatever the house decided as their reward.
items.whatSheLearned: This leadership role has taught me and helped me to see the different sides of leadership. Being a House Minister has helped me build skills like basic public speaking, crowd management, being an advocate for my peers, and having strong communication. From this role I've learnt how to be more confident speaking to a large crowd of known and unknown people, how to manage a noisy crowd, and how to put into action the different changes that students want to see implemented in the school.

images.alt: Rithu in her school uniform, wearing her House Minister badge, in a group photo of the House Ministers
